conventions.convention: Labels are the finite discrete set {1,…,K}, K≥2; classifiers choose the least index attaining the maximum score. Margin loss counts margins ≤γ.

The helper, finite codebook and decoder maps are fixed independently of the sample; the measurable code selector may depend on the sample. There are at most r^q codes, including a singleton empty product for q=0.
Samples have positive integer length and IID observations. Training and selection maps are measurable, and compression succeeds for almost every sample. Logarithms are natural; 0<δ<1 and ε>0.
Coordinatewise distortion ε preserves an observed label when its original margin is strictly greater than 2ε. The probability bound concerns the compressed classifier.
The example supplies a single-sample compression witness and explicitly fails the theorem's almost-sure compression premise.

load_bearing.statement: A fixed-helper finite parameter codebook has nonempty code set A with |A|≤r^q and coordinatewise measurable decoder scores. A measurable sample-dependent selector α compresses f_S on S when the maximum coordinatewise score error is at most ε at every observed input.

Under the stated measurable fixed-codebook setup, IID sampling with m≥1, ε>0, 0<δ<1, and compression on almost every sample, with probability at least 1−δ: R_P(h_{s,α(S)}) ≤ L̂_{2ε}(f_S;S) + sqrt((q log r + log(1/δ))/(2m)).

published_dependencies.used_for: Instance and sample measurable-space conventions.
Product domains, measurable rectangles, coordinate projections and the map S↦(S,X_i).
Preimage arguments for classifiers, selectors, compositions and success events.
Measurability of score comparisons, finite maxima, margins, distortions and empirical averages; all functions used here are finite-valued.
Mutual independence and common observation law.
Finite union bound over the fixed codebook.
Inverse relation exp(log x)=x for positive x.
Positivity of the threshold and rewriting log(r^q/δ), including q=0 and r=1.
Positive Markov thresholds and exponential reciprocal identities.
Centered MGF estimate for each fixed-code zero-one loss, for positive and negative real parameters, without a choice assumption.
Independence of fixed-code loss variables obtained from IID observations.
Factorization of the finite product of nonnegative Borel exponential functions.
One-sided empirical-risk deviation bound using λ=−4t.
Converting the exponential of a finite sum into a product.
Continuity of exponential functions and comparison of tail events.
Continuity of the affine map x↦λ(x−μ).
Continuity of x↦exp(λ(x−μ)).
Deriving Borel measurability of the exponential test functions from open preimages.
Identifying each observation's law with P.
Identifying each fixed-code loss expectation with its integral against P.
Definition of the exponential used in the MGF argument.
Identifying expected zero-one loss with population error probability.

seams_checked.note: Checked the prerequisite page and actual feedforward-network definition against the example's explicit realizations. Its hidden ReLU units, identity outputs, zero output weights and output biases satisfy that interface. The supplier diagram has the stated input-to-hidden-to-output directions. No universal-approximation theorem is invoked.

Checked the prerequisite page and its four item interfaces. Its binary PAC and ERM guarantees serve as context; the compression theorem independently proves the required multiclass one-sided finite-loss bound using published MGF, factorization and Markov suppliers. It does not misapply the binary ERM theorem or import its two-sided constant.
